finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 22-23 contain a Readiness heading and an approval checklist item. Neither directs network discovery or executes a network operation.
Line 18 is prose about FTC opt-out requirements and links to public FTC guidance. The word requests refers to unsubscribe requests, not a Python HTTP library.
Line 18 summarizes sender identification, opt-out deadlines, and message classification. It contains no instruction to inspect a host or enumerate system information.
Line 24 instructs preserving suppression evidence and verifying permission before resubscription. This is audience-safety guidance, not system reconnaissance.
Line 26 describes unsubscribe testing with synthetic contacts and prohibits unnecessary opt-out barriers. These are scoped workflow checks, not host discovery or unauthorized reconnaissance.
Line 11 describes post-purchase message branches for refunds, delivery, and service issues. It does not inspect systems or collect machine information.
Line 14 uses system of record to mean the authoritative source for renewal dates and account state. No host reconnaissance is requested.
Line 18 lists event-contract fields such as event IDs, timestamps, consent references, and validation behavior. This documents application data requirements rather than enumerating host information.
Line 19 links to a consent-to-inbox guide and discusses confirmation and audience routing. It neither imports a configuration library nor reads environment variables or credentials.
Line 28 explains Apple privacy prefetching and security-scanner effects on engagement metrics. It describes measurement limitations, not instructions to scan systems.
Line 32 defines experiment hypotheses, allocation, observation windows, and guardrails. These are measurement-planning requirements with no system reconnaissance behavior.
Lines 5-6 list public FTC and ICO guidance URLs with descriptive titles. They contain no network enumeration commands or target-discovery instructions.
Line 6 documents exit statuses in a module docstring. The reviewed implementation reads one supplied JSON file and reports checklist completeness without system enumeration.

Line 45 uses Markdown backticks for an optional local Python checker and its test command, not executable shell substitution. The reviewed checker parses local JSON without subprocesses, network access, or email sending.
Line 21 lists suppression conditions and distinguishes essential service messages from marketing. It defines recipient eligibility safeguards, not system reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Design and Audit Email Automation Journeys
content.value_statement: Email journeys can send duplicate, poorly timed, or ineligible messages when event rules and ownership are unclear. This skill prepares journey maps, message drafts, suppression rules, and launch checks for your chosen platform.
actual_capabilities: Draft lifecycle journeys with entry events, eligibility, timing, conditional branches, re-entry rules, and conversion exits.
Prepare subjects, preheaders, message outlines or full copy, calls to action, and personalization fallbacks.
Specify event contracts, durable deduplication rules, frequency caps, and handling for late events or unknown send outcomes.
Audit permission evidence, suppression propagation, unsubscribe behavior, and the distinction between marketing and service messages.
Create synthetic QA scenarios, staged launch plans, rollback controls, and conversion-focused measurement plans.
Check a supplied local launch checklist with an optional offline Python helper that reports missing or invalid fields.
limitations: The package provides guidance and a local checklist helper, not a bundled email platform connector or sending service.
Live changes and test sends require suitable access, verified platform features, and explicit authorization.
Legal and provider guidance requires current verification; the skill does not certify compliance or guarantee inbox placement.
The offline helper checks self-reported checklist fields, not actual account configuration, recipient eligibility, or production behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan SaaS onboarding
use_cases.description: Map verified activation events into onboarding steps, with completion exits, missing-event handling, and shared frequency caps.

use_cases.title: Audit cart recovery
use_cases.description: Review checkout eligibility, purchase exits, duplicate events, approved offers, and suppression before activating recovery messages.

use_cases.title: Prepare launch handoff
use_cases.description: Produce event contracts, synthetic test cases, ownership rules, and pause procedures for a platform implementation team.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a welcome journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a welcome journey for [business] and [audience] on [platform]. Include entry rules, messages, timing, suppression, and exits. Mark missing facts and assumptions. Do not change accounts or send messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a platform-neutral first draft.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an existing flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this email flow: [flow details]. Review eligibility, unsubscribe handling, conversion exits, frequency caps, and overlapping journeys. Prioritize fixes and identify evidence needed before launch. Do not activate anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: identify operational gaps in an existing journey.

prompt_templates.title: Specify resilient event handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an implementation specification from [event schema], [journey], and [platform constraints]. Define identity, deduplication, event ordering, re-entry, queue suppression, and unknown-send reconciliation. Include synthetic positive and negative tests. Label proposed event names clearly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: translate a journey into engineering requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a staged experiment launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a staged launch and experiment plan using [approved audience], [journey version], [baseline], and [provider constraints]. Define holdouts, conversion metrics, observation windows, guardrails, backfill checks, and rollback ownership. Separate verified evidence from outstanding checks. Do not send or activate anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate measurement, release controls, and launch approval.

output_examples.input: Draft SaaS onboarding for eligible new accounts, with setup completion as the goal.
output: Entry: verified account creation with documented eligibility. Event names remain proposed until the platform schema is confirmed.
Step 1: welcome message with the next setup action and safe personalization fallbacks.
Step 2: after an approved delay, remind only accounts with incomplete setup.
Exit: stop setup reminders when completion is verified. Recheck suppression before each marketing message.
Status: design only. Timing, platform behavior, and launch authorization remain unverified.

output_examples.input: Audit cart recovery when duplicate events arrive and a purchase can occur before the reminder.
output: Blocker: verify permission and current purchase status before each reminder.
Deduplication: define a durable key for recipient, journey version, step, and qualifying event.
Recovery: reconcile ambiguous provider outcomes before retrying; hold unresolved sends.
QA: test duplicate checkout events, purchase before send, opt-out after enrollment, and late event arrival.
Release: confirm maximum audience, inspect backfill, and assign an owner who can stop queued messages.

best_practices: Supply verified platform details, event fields, permission evidence, and the requested execution scope before implementation.
Test suppression, conversion exits, duplicate events, and unknown send outcomes with synthetic records before an authorized staged launch.
Define conversion metrics, monitoring ownership, stopping thresholds, and queued-message cancellation before activation.
anti_patterns: Treating a journey draft or completed local checklist as permission to activate or send.
Re-enrolling unsubscribed contacts or using a service label to bypass marketing suppression.
Retrying an uncertain send without reconciliation or selecting experiment winners from open rates alone.

faq.question: Does this skill send email automatically?
faq.answer: No bundled sending service is included. External actions require appropriate tools, account access, and authorization.

faq.question: Which email platforms does it support?
faq.answer: The guidance is platform-neutral. Implementation depends on verified account features; optional Poptin notes apply only when relevant.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the business outcome, audience, platform, available events, sending regions, permission evidence, existing flows, cadence limits, and requested scope.

faq.question: Does it certify legal compliance?
faq.answer: No. It distinguishes eligibility, provider rules, and operational readiness, but current requirements and unclear legal questions need qualified review.

faq.question: What does the offline preflight helper verify?
faq.answer: It validates supplied checklist fields and reports outstanding items. It does not inspect accounts, send messages, or prove production readiness.

faq.question: Can it measure incremental impact?
faq.answer: It can propose randomized holdouts and conversion-based metrics. Credible lift estimates still require suitable data, stable assignment, and contamination controls.
